interactions.teaches: The scale of the recovery. Pipe count and water pressure grow with depth, and familiar landmarks fall far short of the wreck.
interactions.studentAction: Drag the winch slider or press Lower it to the wreck.
interactions.feedback: The claw moves down the water column, four readouts update, and a line names the last landmark passed.
interactions.staticFallback: A noscript paragraph gives the pipe count and pressure at the wreck.
interactions.identityFit: The control is the ship's winch and the readouts use the typewriter face of the documents.

interactions.teaches: What a cover story demands. Every answer had to match what the world already believed about the ship.
interactions.studentAction: Choose a reply to each of four Soviet questions.
interactions.feedback: Each choice explains why it would hold or break the cover, then the real reply from the CIA transcript is logged.
interactions.staticFallback: A noscript paragraph prints the real exchange.
interactions.identityFit: The radio log is set in typewriter type with Soviet red and sonar teal speakers.

interactions.teaches: What the CIA got compared with what it wanted, and where the evidence is still disputed.
interactions.studentAction: Tap each part of the submarine on the drawing or the buttons.
interactions.feedback: The chosen part highlights and a status reports whether it reached the ship, fell back, or was never grabbed.
interactions.staticFallback: A legend colors every part and a noscript paragraph lists all four outcomes.
interactions.identityFit: A damage report on the hull drawing in the same three colors used across the hub.

interactions.teaches: What the operation and the burial actually looked like.
interactions.studentAction: Press play on a video inside the page.
interactions.feedback: The YouTube player starts inside the page.
interactions.staticFallback: Each video has an Open on YouTube link.
interactions.identityFit: Footage sits beside the moment it shows.
